title: A Compass for the Passage
premise: Desert ranger Sable Coldharbour chases a thief into the drowned lowlands and instead finds a chest bearing the seal of Vessia, a nation erased from maps forty years ago. The chest holds a compass that points not north but toward what the bearer has lost, and the salvage fleet that rules the river will kill to own it. Hunted by the fleet's admiral — his mother's old commander, who helped erase Vessia to bury her own crimes — Sable gathers a found crew of castoffs and follows the compass to the sunken capital itself. In the flooded archive beneath the wreck he must choose between restoring a dead nation's truth and protecting the living family he never expected to have; he burns the compass, publishes the truth, and lets the past stay drowned.
about_author: Isandro Coldharbour is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent six seasons mapping channels through drowned settlements before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about landscapes that remember more than the people crossing them.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Stole Nothing
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Tracking a thief across hardpan desert, Sable catches him at the river's edge only to watch him drown clutching nothing worth dying for. Searching the body, Sable finds a scrap of salvage chart marked with a symbol he half-remembers from childhood stories. The beat is unease: the wilderness gave him his quarry, but not the answer.

chapters.title: What the River Gives Up
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. After a storm flood recedes, the river exposes an iron chest stamped with Vessia's seal — a nation Sable was taught never existed. Inside lies a brass compass whose needle ignores north and swings toward something upstream. The emotional beat is wonder curdling into dread as he realizes the chest was buried deliberately, and someone paid to keep it hidden.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, ending on the antagonist's. A harbor informer tells him the Meridian salvage fleet has posted a bounty on exactly such a chest, and that the fleet reaches the wreck site in six tides. Sable decides to race them. Final scene shifts to Admiral Corvane Ash, who receives word the compass surfaced — and orders no witnesses left alive. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: A Crew of Castoffs
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Unable to sail alone, Sable recruits three rejects: Wren, a disgraced cartographer who recognizes the compass's craft; Brannoc, a defected fleet diver; and Pip, an orphan stowaway who refuses to leave. Their bickering aboard a leaky skiff forms the first fragile bonds. Beat: reluctant loner learns he cannot outrun the fleet — or his loneliness — alone.

chapters.title: The Needle Turns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Studying the compass, Wren discovers it points toward what its holder has lost, not a place — and for Sable it bends toward a village he fled as a boy. Flashbacks reveal Sable's mother was Vessian, disappeared during the erasure. Beat: the quest becomes personal; grief surfaces that the desert taught him to bury.

chapters.title: The Fleet's Shadow
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The fleet catches them at a trading reach; Brannoc's knowledge of their signals buys an escape through a burning customs station, but Pip is briefly taken and returned with a message from Ash: surrender the compass and live. Sable refuses. Beat: first blood, first real cost, and the crew stops being passengers and becomes a family under fire.

chapters.title: The Drowned Capital
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Guided by the needle, they reach Vessia's sunken capital on the fifth tide — spires beneath green water, streets where fish school through doorways. Pip, diving with Brannoc, finds the archive entrance but triggers an old fleet mooring line; Ash's flagship appears on the horizon. Beat: awe and terror entwined; the past is beautiful and it is a trap.

chapters.title: Ash's Bargain
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable and Ash POV. Boarded before they can dive, Sable confronts Ash, who reveals she served beside Sable's mother and helped erase Vessia to conceal a massacre she ordered. She offers Sable command, legacy, power — everything the compass could restore. Beat: temptation at its peak; Sable sees how easily grief becomes ambition, the corruption the theme demands.

chapters.title: The Archive Below
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Feigning acceptance, Sable dives with Wren while Brannoc sabotages the flagship. In the flooded archive they find the full record of the massacre — and Sable understands the compass was built so the truth could always be found again. Ash corners him among the shelves; Pip's warning dive saves his life as the sabotage erupts above. Beat: climax — truth won at the edge of drowning.

chapters.title: Let the Past Stay Drowned
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. With Ash's flagship sinking and Ash herself refusing rescue, Sable chooses not to become Vessia's avenger-king: he breaks the compass, scatters its pages of proof to every port, and sails home with Wren, Brannoc, and Pip. The final image is the four of them charting new water together. Beat: resolution — memory honored without being worshipped; power refused; family chosen.
